description: Jeddah Junior Astronauts: a Jeddah team of educators and coders building a fun space-mission trainer with NASA open data to teach kids coding, robotics, and AI. Beginners welcome! Arabic & English.
summary: Postcards from the Left Behind is an interactive storytelling website for school-age space enthusiasts. Nine machines that NASA left on the Moon and Mars each write a postcard home to a student on Earth, in their own voice: the Apollo 11 laser mirror, Surveyor 3, the Apollo science stations, the Apollo 17 rover, Viking 1, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Ingenuity. Every postcard has a story, a real address in latitude and longitude, and the science the machine made possible. Students read or listen to a postcard, find the machine on a map of real landing sites, collect its stamp, solve "Who am I?" clues, and write a postcard back. A chart shows how many times each Mars machine outlived its planned mission. The site is made for students aged 9 to 14, works in English and Arabic, and includes a 50-minute lesson plan, so this hardware is remembered for what it taught us.
details:
The problem

Since the 1960s NASA has left hardware on the Moon and Mars. NASA's own catalogue lists nearly 800 objects on the Moon alone. Students meet these machines as lists of names and dates, and the science they made possible stays hidden.

Our idea

Nine machines write a postcard home to a student on Earth, in their own voice. Each postcard has a story, a real address in latitude and longitude, and the science the machine made possible. It is made for students aged 9 to 14, who can add their own drawings to every postcard.

How it works

1. Read a postcard from the Moon or Mars, or listen to it read aloud.

2. Find the machine's address on the map of real landing sites.

3. Collect its stamp, then solve the "Who am I?" clues.

4. Write back: send your own postcard to the machine.

NASA data inside

Landing coordinates and mission dates come from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive. Planned and actual lifetimes come from NASA's Mars mission records. Every postcard links to its official NASA record. A chart shows how many times longer than planned each machine worked: Opportunity 57 times, Viking 1 and Spirit 25 times, Ingenuity 14 times, Sojourner 12 times.

Impact

Ready for class: a 50-minute lesson plan for ages 9 to 14 is built into the page. Two languages, English and Arabic, so students in our region read it in their own language. Free and simple: it runs in any browser, with read-aloud for younger readers.

Tools

HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single page, inline SVG for the map and pictures, the browser Web Speech API for read aloud, and browser local storage for stamps, replies and drawings. No server and no login.

What comes next

More postcards from machines in deep space and from other space agencies, and a gallery of postcards and drawings sent in by students.

Use of AI

An AI assistant (Claude) helped with the code, the first-draft text, the page design, the placeholder pictures and the slides. Placeholder pictures are marked "AI-generated placeholder". The team checks the facts against NASA sources and adds its own drawings.
